data.body:
Recurrence observed 2026-09-20, ~10:05 UTC, during the overnight bug sweep.

Three separate pushes from three unrelated linked worktrees of
`/Users/joeoakhart/rebar` were rejected back-to-back with the same object:

```
error: remote unpack failed: error Missing tree 9f4ab41bab6e47afe5f45f59209751fc83c40e6f
 ! [remote rejected]  HEAD -> refs/for/main%hashtag=... (n/a (unpacker error))
```

The three worktrees carried unrelated changes (`c6fb` gate-sidecar visibility,
`859c` Terraform variable defaults, `974f` mirror-guard lag tolerance) on two
different bases (`9db00e4cf8d` and `0bce6a72425`), so the common factor was the
remote, not any one patch.

Client-side state at the time, which rules out the local repository:

- `git cat-file -t 9f4ab41bab6e47afe5f45f59209751fc83c40e6f` returns `tree`.
- The repository is not a partial clone: `remote.origin.promisor` and
  `remote.*.partialclonefilter` are unset, `core.repositoryformatversion` is `0`.
- The tree is reachable from `origin/main`, and is the `tests` tree of
  `740983fe830`.

Server-side the object should have been present: the stale
`refs/remotes/gerrit/main` at the time was `1f338f2c57e` ("Preserve partial
metered Bedrock spend"), which *is* an ancestor of `origin/main`, and
`git rev-list --objects 1f338f2c57e` contains `9f4ab41` — so the tree was
reachable from a commit Gerrit had already merged.

Resolution without repair. I ran `git fetch gerrit` (a read, no mutation), which
advanced `refs/remotes/gerrit/main` from `1f338f2c57e` to `c0b1ad2e8e9`, then
retried. All three pushes then succeeded immediately, opening changes 3005, 3006
and 3007. No EBS snapshot, no mirror-fetch into the Gerrit bare repo, and no
ownership normalization were performed.

What this does and does not establish. It does NOT confirm the ownership root
cause recorded in the final RCA, because no root-owned repair was run tonight and
no server state was touched. It is consistent with hypothesis C from the original
RCA — a transient visibility window around recently merged objects — since the
window here immediately followed three submits in quick succession (3002, 3003,
3004 merged as `d08a0a373a3`, `740983fe830`, `c0b1ad2e8e9`), and `9f4ab41` belongs
to one of exactly those just-merged commits.

I cannot separate "the fetch fixed push negotiation" from "the transient window
closed on its own during the retry", because both happened in the same step. That
ambiguity is recorded rather than resolved; establishing which requires catching a
recurrence and retrying WITHOUT an intervening fetch.

Recording here rather than reopening: this ticket is closed, the recurrence needed
no server-side repair, and the sweep was unblocked. Flagging for an operator
decision on whether the recurrence warrants its own ticket.
